nodes.label: Deviation 1: No SSR — Static Export + OG Meta Service
nodes.rationale: The blueprint chose SSR purely for Instagram/Telegram link previews. A static export plus a small dedicated OG meta service that serves crawler-facing tags recovers the preview benefit without running a Node runtime for the app itself.

nodes.label: Deviation 2: RabbitMQ, Not BullMQ
nodes.rationale: RabbitMQ gives a real dead-letter topology, per-queue routing and backoff exchanges that BullMQ-on-Redis does not. Redis stays, but only for cache and the FX snapshot — never as a queue.

nodes.label: Deviation 3: Back Office in Next.js, Not React+Vite
nodes.rationale: One toolchain and one generated API client across both surfaces beats a second bundler and a second client for a data-dense internal tool.

nodes.label: Port Proxy Chain (cache → breaker → retry → timeout → instrumentation → adapter)
nodes.rationale: Every outbound third-party call goes through a port and every port is wrapped in the same decorator chain, so resilience and observability are structural rather than per-call discipline. Calling an SDK or fetch directly from a service bypasses all of it.

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox + Event-Only Cross-Module Communication
nodes.rationale: Domain events are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and then relayed to RabbitMQ. Events cross module boundaries and direct cross-module calls do not — this is precisely what makes later extraction into services possible.

nodes.label: Composition Root as the Only Adapter-Aware Place
nodes.rationale: If swapping an adapter requires touching the core, the change is wrong. Keeping provider names in exactly one file is the enforcement mechanism for the whole ports-and-adapters bet.

nodes.label: Multi-Provider Registry + Failover Chain
nodes.rationale: Payment, identity, FX and SMS are multi-provider by default behind one port, so adding a provider means one adapter plus one registry entry and nothing else.

nodes.label: Cache-Aside with Single-Flight and TTL Jitter
nodes.rationale: Third-party reads and expensive joins go through the shared cache package rather than ad-hoc Redis calls, so single-flight stampede protection, TTL jitter and negative caching apply uniformly.

nodes.label: INVARIANT: Payment ≠ Purchased
nodes.rationale: A successful gateway charge means the customer's money is held; it says nothing about whether the foreign purchase succeeded. Collapsing PAID into PURCHASED is treated as a correctness bug, not a simplification.

nodes.label: INVARIANT: Max-Procurement-Price Guard
nodes.rationale: If the live marketplace price at purchase time exceeds the quote's maxProcurementPrice the order branches to PRICE_CHANGED. The guard exists so the system never makes a silent negative-margin purchase; the check is against a live offer immediately before buying.

nodes.label: INVARIANT: Viability Gate at Order Creation
Persian-First RTL, Bilingual fa/en Validation Errors
nodes.rationale: Customer-facing strings are Persian and the UI is RTL by default, but validation errors are returned in both fa and en so the client picks — the API never has to guess the caller's locale.

nodes.label: @xb/contracts Zod Schemas as Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Request/response validation, generated types and the frontend client all derive from the same Zod schemas, so front end and back end cannot drift.
